title: 5 m + 5 s? Dimensions Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Five apples plus five apples is ten apples. But Aarav rides 5 metres in 5 seconds, writes 5 m + 5 s, and his calculator says 10. Ten what? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn what the dimensions of a physical quantity are, and why only quantities with the same dimensions can be added.

Ride with Aarav on a live motion notebook: the bicycle, its readout and two graphs move together, a slow-mo replay grows the velocity and acceleration vectors, and the slopes show why speed is [LT⁻¹] and acceleration is [LT⁻²]. We build the dimensions of area, volume and density step by step, compare distance and time side by side, meet dimensionless quantities (angle and strain), work out momentum [MLT⁻¹], see the exam trap about the radian, solve an original NEET pattern question, and end with a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Same kind only: 5 m + 5 s?
0:26 What dimensions are: [M], [L], [T]
0:48 Aarav's ride: speed [LT⁻¹] and acceleration [LT⁻²], live
1:29 Dimensions of area, step by step
2:01 Volume and density, link by link
2:33 Side by side + pause and think
3:07 Same dimensions, or none: angle, frequency, strain
3:44 Worked example: momentum [MLT⁻¹]
4:16 Exam trap: no dimension does not mean no unit
4:35 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:12 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Dimensional Formulae. What is pressure made of, in M, L and T?
